item.title: auto silently skips items with missing or too-short intent — no feedback to user
item.intent: When auto-pick bypasses items due to missing or insufficient intent, a warning must be logged identifying each skipped item by ID and stating the reason, so users can fix their backlog.
item.description: pick_item silently skips items where intent is absent or under 20 characters. In an auto session with multiple unready items, the user sees no items processed and no explanation. This makes the intent gate invisible: users don't know why their backlog isn't draining. A targeted log_warn call when each item is bypassed for intent reasons closes the feedback loop.
steps: In pick_item, when an item is rejected due to missing or too-short intent, emit: log_warn "Skipping $id: intent missing or too short (9 chars, need >=20)"
Verify the same path is covered in list_pickable_ids if that function also filters by intent
Run shellcheck and verify no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Running auto with items whose intent is absent or under 20 chars produces a warning line per skipped item identifying the ID and reason
Items with valid intent are still processed normally — no regression
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
